harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1's root crontab to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15, appending output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. The script file was found corrupted (leftover heredoc text) and was rewritten to a working POSIX sh script, made executable, and functionally verified. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and cron/log health, issued a self-acknowledging systemctl reboot, polled until the node returned, proved the boot_id changed, and confirmed cron service, crontab entry, script, and log file all survived and continued to function post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and found it corrupted with leftover heredoc/shell text
Rewrote the script to a correct POSIX sh script and set ownership root:root, mode 0755
Ran the script manually to confirm it produces expected output
Added a root crontab entry: 15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1
Manually ran the exact crontab command line to confirm it appends correctly to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
Confirmed cron.service is enabled and active on node1
Captured baseline boot_id and health (cron active, crontab present, log content) before restart
Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, observing connection reset/timeout during the restart window
Verified boot_id changed after restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified cron active/enabled, crontab entry intact, script intact and executable, and prior log entry preserved post-restart
Re-ran the maintenance command post-restart to confirm continued correct append behavior

evidence.summary: Found script corrupted, rewrote it to a valid POSIX sh script with 0755 perms, and confirmed it runs and prints the expected inventory line.

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled for 02:15 daily writing to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Installed root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' and manually executed the exact command line, confirming output is correctly appended to the log file.

evidence.requirement: Cron daemon active/enabled so schedule will actually fire
evidence.summary: systemctl showed cron.service enabled and active (running) on node1.
Captured boot_id, uptime, cron active status, crontab contents, and log contents prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 1 && systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, then subsequent execs failed with connection reset/timeout confirming the node went down.

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id (011daef2-2b82-41e2-bc08-230e5d870eea) differs from baseline boot_id (cfdbaef8-7705-46ed-b0cd-c985235704ea), proving an actual kernel restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 required services and data recovered after restart
evidence.summary: After restart, cron.service is active/enabled, the crontab entry and script remain intact/executable, the prior log entry persisted, and re-running the job appended a new line successfully.
